definition: Google Assistant is a discontinued virtual assistant software application developed by Google that is primarily available on home automation and mobile devices.
details: Based on artificial intelligence, Google Assistant can engage in two-way conversations, unlike the company's previous virtual assistant, Google Now. Google Assistant debuted in 2016 as part of Google's messaging app Allo, and its voice-activated speaker Google Nest. After a period of exclusivity on the Google Pixel smartphones, it was deployed on other Android devices starting in February 2017, including third-party smartphones and Android Wear (now Wear OS), and was released as a standalone app on the iOS operating system in May 2017. Alongside the announcement of a software development kit in April 2017, Assistant has been further extended to support a large variety of devices, including cars and third-party smart home appliances. The functionality of Assistant can also be enhanced by third-party developers. At CES 2018, the first Assistant-powered smart displays (smart speakers with video screens) were announced, with the first one being released in July 2018. In 2020, Google Assistant was already available on more than 1 billion devices. Users primarily interact with Google Assistant through natural voice, though keyboard input is also supported. explainer.lead: Google Assistant was Google's voice- and text-controlled helper for answering questions, managing everyday tasks, and operating devices. Its two-way conversations made it more interactive than Google Now, and its reach extended from phones to speakers, cars, wearables, and smart-home appliances before Gemini largely replaced it.

tiers.eli5: Google Assistant was like a helpful receptionist living inside a phone, speaker, car, or appliance. You could ask it a question or tell it to set an alarm, and it could answer and continue the conversation instead of handling only one command. It arrived in 2016, and in 2026 Google shut it down for mobile users and pointed them toward Gemini, although Assistant remained on some older and not-yet-transitioned devices.
tiers.practitioner: Developers extended Assistant through Actions on Google, launched in December 2016, while the April 2017 SDK let hardware makers embed it in products such as Raspberry Pi systems, cars, and home appliances. Integrations had to account for both speech and typed input, device-specific capabilities, account and hardware permissions, and an expanding but uneven range of supported platforms. Its replacement by Gemini makes platform and migration status a central concern for maintaining Assistant-dependent experiences.
tiers.paperLevel: Google Assistant was an AI-based virtual-assistant application and cloud service that accepted natural voice or keyboard input and produced answers or actions, including web search, event and alarm scheduling, hardware adjustment, Google-account information retrieval, and games. Unlike Google Now, it supported two-way conversation using Google's natural-language processing algorithm, with later capabilities including camera-based object identification, purchases, and money transfers. It was a deployed product rather than a named formal model, and its functions and availability varied across devices before its large-scale replacement by Gemini.

explainer.example: A user says, “Set an alarm for 7 a.m.” Assistant interprets the spoken request, schedules the alarm on the user's device, and confirms the result; because it supports two-way conversation, the interaction can continue with another request rather than ending after a search result.

usedIn.name: Allo and Google Nest
usedIn.detail: Assistant debuted in 2016 within Google's Allo messaging app and its voice-activated Google Nest speaker.

usedIn.name: Android and iOS devices
usedIn.detail: After an initial Pixel-phone exclusive period, it expanded across Android and became a separate iOS app in May 2017.

usedIn.name: Smart displays
usedIn.detail: Assistant-powered displays from Lenovo, Sony, JBL, and LG combined voice assistance with video calls, videos, maps, calendars, and camera footage.

usedIn.name: Cars and home automation
usedIn.detail: The developer SDK supported integration into Audi and Volvo cars and appliances including fridges, washers, and ovens.

explainer.intuition: Assistant turned spoken or typed requests into useful actions across Google's services and connected devices. Its key advance over Google Now was conversational interaction: a user could exchange messages with it rather than merely receive information or issue isolated commands.
howItWorks: A user speaks naturally or types a request into a supported device.
Assistant processes the request using Google's natural-language processing technology.
It searches for information, retrieves permitted Google-account details, or selects a device or service action.
It returns an answer, visual card, or spoken response, or carries out tasks such as setting an alarm.
Optional developer-built Actions and SDK integrations extend the same interaction to additional apps and hardware.
explainer.whyItMatters: Assistant brought conversational control to a unusually broad consumer ecosystem, reaching more than 1 billion devices and over 500 million monthly users by 2020. Its developer platform also showed how a single assistant could connect search, personal accounts, mobile software, vehicles, and household hardware.
misconceptions: It was not simply Google Now renamed: two-way conversation distinguished Assistant from Google's earlier assistant.
It was not only a smart-speaker feature; phones, tablets, wearables, laptops, cars, displays, and appliances also supported it.
Assistant and Gemini are not the same product: Gemini is the LLM-based chatbot that largely replaced Assistant.
